title: Narrow-band random fatigue and the Rayleigh closed form
source: Dirlik and Benasciutti, Metals 11 (2021) 1333, equations (1), (2) and (5); the Rayleigh peak integral is evaluated directly from the four moments.

quantities.reason: A unit-force rod with negligible inertia has unit axial stress transfer. The independent rectangular spectrum is 4 Pa²/Hz on 1..3 Hz, so m0=4(3-1)=8; quadrature error and the tiny retained rod inertia are below the stated band.
For the same rectangle, m2=(4/3)(3³-1³)=104/3, so the Rayleigh zero-crossing rate is sqrt(m2/m0).
With N=100(2/a)^2, Rayleigh E[a²]=2m0, and rate sqrt(m2/m0), D=T rate (2m0/2²)/100 = 0.4 sqrt(13/3).
